stem:
Meena looks at a small printed word in her textbook by holding a convex lens close to the page. Later she holds a flat transparent glass pane over the same word.
How does the word appear through each material?

options.text: The word appears erect and enlarged through the convex lens, but the same size and shape through the flat glass pane.
The word appears erect and enlarged through both the convex lens and the flat glass pane.
The word appears smaller through the convex lens, but the same size and shape through the flat glass pane.
The word appears inverted through the flat glass pane, but erect and enlarged through the convex lens.

teacher.key_rationale: A convex lens held close to a nearby object (object within focal length) gives an erect, enlarged image, acting as a magnifying glass; a flat transparent glass pane transmits light without convergence or divergence, so the object looks the same size and shape. B wrongly assumes all transparent materials magnify equally, C reverses the lens effect, D wrongly assigns inversion to flat glass.
